articles.title: Non-Wetted Piezoelectric Vortex Sensor
articles.summary: Keeps the piezoelectric element outside direct media contact while retaining the vortex signal.
articles.introduction: This sensing structure separates the piezoelectric element from direct process contact while preserving the mechanical path used to detect vortex shedding.

image.alt: Velomac non-wetted piezoelectric vortex sensor waveform comparison

sections.title: Why It Matters
paragraphs: A vortex sensor must receive a clear mechanical signal while operating close to process heat, pressure and impurities. Direct media contact can increase the service burden in high-temperature or contamination-prone lines.
Moving the piezoelectric element away from the medium only works when the transmission path still retains a usable vortex signal.

sections.title: Velomac Approach
paragraphs: A thin metal diaphragm and rigid tapered coupling path transfer fluid-induced vibration to a removable sensor core outside direct contact with the process medium.
The protective tube length can be configured to separate the sensing element from the hottest part of the installation.

image.alt: Section view of the removable non-wetted vortex sensor structure

sections.title: Key Technical Points
paragraphs: The current development supports process temperatures above 400°C and reduces direct exposure of the piezoelectric element to deposits and particles.
bullets: More than 95% signal amplitude retained at the confirmed comparison point
Sensor-core service without removing the complete meter body
Field replacement requires the approved isolation and pressure-safety procedure

sections.title: Validation Data
paragraphs: The non-wetted sensor and a traditional medium-contact sensor were compared using the same signal-processing board at one controlled operating point.

rows: More than 95% of the traditional sensor signal amplitude retained

sections.title: Application Value
paragraphs: The structure is relevant to high-temperature steam, thermal process systems, contamination-prone media and continuous lines where removing the full meter body would create significant service work.
Selection still depends on medium, flow range, pressure, temperature, pipe size, vibration and the permitted maintenance procedure.

articles.title: Wide-Turndown Anti-Vibration Vortex Flow Meter
articles.summary: Adaptive filtering and wide flow coverage for pipelines affected by changing load and vibration.
articles.introduction: This vortex flowmeter development addresses two conditions that often occur together: a wide change in operating flow and mechanical vibration from pumps, compressors or nearby equipment.

image.alt: Wide-turndown anti-vibration vortex flowmeter measurement concept

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The meter combines wide flow coverage with adaptive filtering and digital signal-feature analysis. The objective is to retain low-flow vortex information while reducing interference that is unrelated to actual flow.
The current configuration is documented with a maximum turndown ratio of 1:70, coverage from 1% to 100% of rated flow and Class 0.5 measurement.

sections.title: Flow Range Challenge
paragraphs: A fixed filter can suppress useful vortex signals at low velocity, while at higher velocity the vortex frequency may overlap with mechanical vibration or electrical interference.
A wider operating range therefore requires signal handling that can follow the process rather than applying one fixed cutoff across every condition.

sections.title: Vibration Environment
paragraphs: Pipeline vibration often appears as low-frequency narrow-band interference from a few hertz to several hundred hertz. Motors and electrical systems can add fixed-frequency harmonics.
At low flow, vibration amplitude can be larger than the real vortex signal and may create a false flow output if it is not separated correctly.

sections.title: Technical Design
paragraphs: The signal path combines adaptive filtering with digital feature analysis. Ten anti-vibration modes are available so the processing can be matched to the observed site signal.
The design is intended to distinguish persistent mechanical interference from the frequency behavior expected from real vortex shedding.

sections.title: Test Method
paragraphs: A representative program compared measurement behavior with digital signal-feature analysis disabled and enabled under both static and flowing conditions.

sections.title: Test Results
paragraphs: The results below compare the same test condition before and after digital signal-feature analysis was enabled.

sections.title: Suitable Applications
paragraphs: Typical review points include pump areas, compressor lines, utility headers, fluctuating production loads and pipelines with documented mechanical vibration.
A selection review should include minimum, normal and maximum flow, pipe size, medium, pressure, temperature, vibration information and available straight pipe.

articles.title: Electromagnetic Flow Meter with Remote Pressure Monitoring
articles.summary: Combines electromagnetic flow, pressure sensing and 4G access at one liquid measurement point.
articles.introduction: This electromagnetic flowmeter configuration brings flow measurement, pressure sensing and remote communication together at one pipeline location.

image.alt: Electromagnetic flowmeter configured with integrated pressure sensing

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Many pump stations, water systems and process skids need both flow and pressure at the same location. A conventional arrangement uses separate instruments, process connections, wiring and data channels.
The integrated configuration is intended to reduce that installation burden while keeping the two operating variables aligned in time and location.

sections.title: Integrated Pressure Monitoring
paragraphs: The pressure-sensing structure is developed for conditions where pulsation from pumps or reciprocating equipment can repeatedly load the sensing diaphragm.
Pressure range, process connection, material compatibility and pulsation condition must be confirmed for each application.

sections.title: Remote Data Access
paragraphs: An integrated 4G connection supports remote access to operating data without adding a separate wireless transmission unit.
Network coverage, data destination, update interval and protocol requirements should be reviewed during configuration.

sections.title: System Structure
paragraphs: The configuration combines an electromagnetic flow sensor, a pressure sensing point, local conversion and display, and a remote communication module.
bullets: Pressure reading at the same pipeline location
Local display and electrical output configuration

sections.title: Application Scenarios
paragraphs: Typical scenarios include distributed pump stations, water and wastewater networks, integrated treatment equipment, chemical batching systems and packaged skids with limited installation space.
The configuration is most useful when both flow and pressure are required for pump review, line condition monitoring or remote operation.

sections.title: Operational Value
paragraphs: Co-located readings make it easier to compare pressure and flow behavior at the same point. The integrated arrangement can also reduce separate process openings, wiring runs and field devices.
Selection still starts with liquid conductivity, lining and electrode compatibility, pipe size, flow range, pressure, temperature, communication and power supply.

articles.title: Velomac-Developed Liquid Flow Calibration Bench
articles.summary: An in-house circulation and control platform supporting the master-meter method.
articles.introduction: An in-house developed circulation and control platform supporting liquid flow-point adjustment, reference-meter comparison and recorded verification.

image.alt: Velomac-developed liquid flow calibration bench and pipeline connections

sections.title: System Overview
paragraphs: The self-developed bench combines a stainless steel telescopic volumetric tube, operating as a piston displacement device, with an electronic scale.
The displacement system establishes a reference liquid volume while the scale records the mass of the discharged liquid. These two measurements provide a connected check of the flowmeter under test.

sections.title: Why Velomac Developed It
paragraphs: Liquid is effectively incompressible under the bench operating principle, allowing displaced volume and measured mass to be compared directly.
Using both references supports cross-checking of accumulated flow and instantaneous flow rather than relying on one measurement method alone.

sections.title: Calibration Process
paragraphs: Extending the telescopic tube increases its internal volume and draws in a defined quantity of liquid. Controlled retraction then discharges that reference volume through the flowmeter under test.
During discharge, the electronic scale measures the actual liquid mass. The displaced volume, measured mass and flowmeter output can then be compared as part of the calibration review.

sections.title: Measurement Range
paragraphs: The displacement travel determines the reference liquid volume, while the controlled retraction speed determines the reference flow rate.
Applicable bench capacity and configured flow points are confirmed for the meter under review rather than presented as one fixed range for every configuration.

sections.title: Test Points
paragraphs: Reference points can be established by controlling the displacement travel and retraction speed. This allows the bench to present defined liquid volumes and flow conditions to the meter.
The required minimum, normal and maximum flow should be provided so suitable test points can be reviewed before calibration.

sections.title: Control and Data Collection
paragraphs: Reference volume is derived from the displacement of the telescopic tube and liquid mass is recorded by the scale. The two values can also be used to calculate density using ρ = m / V.

The calculated reference values are compared with the flowmeter's accumulated and instantaneous flow readings. Report format and any electrical output checks should be confirmed with the quotation requirements.

sections.title: Application Value
paragraphs: The volume-and-mass method provides two related references for reviewing liquid flowmeter output and helps keep calibration work close to manufacturing and configuration.
For a useful review, send the medium, pipe size, minimum and maximum flow, pressure, temperature, connection, power and signal requirements.

articles.title: Vibration Measurement Test System
articles.summary: Applies controlled airflow and mechanical vibration while recording the meter response.
articles.introduction: The test system combines a controlled airflow path with a vibration motor, vibration sensor and coordinated data collection so meter behavior can be reviewed under flow and vibration at the same time.

image.alt: Velomac vibration measurement test system concept

sections.title: System Overview
paragraphs: The system brings an airflow circuit, vibration source and measurement instruments onto one test platform. The arrangement is intended to reproduce a controlled flow condition while mechanical vibration is applied close to the meter.
This allows the response of an anti-vibration flowmeter to be observed under a condition that a conventional no-vibration flow check does not reproduce.

image.alt: Structure diagram of the Velomac vibration measurement test system

sections.title: Test Purpose
paragraphs: Industrial flowmeters may operate near pumps, motors, compressors and vibrating pipework. A meter can pass a normal flow check yet show false output or increased variation when mechanical disturbance is added.
The system is used to compare flow signal behavior while the vibration condition is known and recorded.

sections.title: Vibration Conditions
paragraphs: A vibration motor applies disturbance near the meter while a vibration sensor records the actual condition around the sensing area.
One representative anti-vibration test program used approximately 1g three-axis acceleration for about five minutes. Other conditions require a defined test plan.

sections.title: Test Procedure
paragraphs: The blower establishes airflow through the sealed line and the electric regulating valve sets the required flow. After the flow stabilizes, the vibration motor is operated and the vibration sensor records the applied condition.
Meter output and system status are collected at the same time so the effect of vibration can be compared against the controlled flow condition.
bullets: Record vibration and meter output together

sections.title: Data Collection
paragraphs: The PLC and software interface can collect vibration frequency, instantaneous flow, accumulated flow, regulating valve opening and blower operating status.
Coordinated collection helps relate an observed meter change to the applied vibration and flow condition.

sections.title: Validation Value
paragraphs: The system supports product development, anti-vibration mode comparison and pre-shipment technical review for applications where vibration is a known site condition.
It does not replace a site assessment. Buyers should still share the source of vibration, approximate frequency or acceleration when known, pipe supports, flow range and installation layout.

seo.title: Vibration Measurement Test System | Velomac
seo.description: Velomac in-house vibration measurement test system for controlled airflow, applied vibration and coordinated flowmeter data collection.

articles.title: Smart Vortex Upgrade for Chemical and Pharmaceutical Processes
articles.summary: Reviews when a vortex meter can replace an orifice plate in chemical and pharmaceutical utility lines.
articles.introduction: This engineering approach evaluates where a vortex flowmeter can reduce the installation and operating burden of an existing orifice plate measurement point in chemical and pharmaceutical utilities.

image.alt: Vortex flowmeter installed on a chemical or pharmaceutical process utility line

sections.title: Operating Challenge
paragraphs: Chemical and pharmaceutical plants often operate across changing batch loads, utility demand and production schedules. A narrow measurement range can reduce low-load visibility, while permanent pressure loss increases the work required from pumps, compressors or boilers.
Hygiene, impulse-line maintenance, available straight pipe and signal traceability can also affect whether the existing measurement point remains suitable.

sections.title: Existing Measurement Method
paragraphs: An orifice plate creates a differential pressure by restricting the flow path. The arrangement normally includes pressure tapping, impulse lines and a differential-pressure transmitter.
The method remains suitable for many installations, but each upgrade review should consider permanent pressure loss, rangeability, impulse-line maintenance and the available installation geometry.

sections.title: Engineering Assessment
paragraphs: The first step is to confirm the real operating envelope rather than selecting a replacement from pipe size alone.
bullets: Pipe size and available straight length

sections.title: Vortex Upgrade Approach
paragraphs: A vortex meter measures the frequency generated as the fluid passes a bluff body. The approach removes the separate impulse-line arrangement and can reduce permanent pressure loss compared with an orifice plate.
Integrated temperature and pressure compensation can be configured when mass or standard-condition reporting is required.

sections.title: Installation Considerations
paragraphs: The replacement point must still be reviewed for upstream disturbance, straight pipe, pipe stress, vibration, condensate behavior, orientation and maintenance access.
For pharmaceutical utilities, wetted material, sanitary connection, surface finish, drainability and cleaning procedure must be confirmed before configuration.

sections.title: Comparison Data
paragraphs: The engineering comparison below records the stated basis used for the reviewed upgrade. Results are application-specific and should be checked against the actual orifice design and process condition.

sections.title: Application Value
paragraphs: A suitable upgrade can improve low-load visibility, reduce pressure-loss burden and simplify the measurement assembly. The value depends on the operating range, utility cost, maintenance history and available installation space.
A recommendation requires the existing orifice data, pipe size, medium, flow range, pressure, temperature, straight pipe, connection and required output.
